newsitem.title: USA: Summers says Japan must seek demand-led recovery.
newsitem.headline: Summers says Japan must seek demand-led recovery.

text.p: Japan should foster demand-led recovery at home and avoid running up external surpluses that would hurt global growth, U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Tuesday.

In a speech prepared for delivery to a trade group in Denver, Colorado, focusing on the coming summit of industrial nations there on June 20-22, Summers said Japan was "just starting to emerge from five years of economic trauma."
He urged Japan to keep up efforts to get rid of stifling regulations and to open its markets to foreign products.
A text of Summers' remarks was released in Washington.
He said the Group of Seven industrial countries -- the United States, Canada, Germany, Britain, Japan, France and Italy -- face greatly different challenges as they approach the summit.
Russia also will attend much of the summit.

Summers said that the United States was "in an extremely strong position" as the world's only military and global superpower. But Europe finds itself "in the midst of a complex economic and political transition" that complicates efforts to achieve the monetary union evisioned by the Maastricht treaty, he said.

Summers said the ultimate success of Europe's bid to create a single currency will depend on dealing with structural problems that have driven unemployment to the highest levels in more than a generation.

Solid progress should flow from the Denver summit in several areas, Summers said. For example, it will build upon efforts at the Halifax summit two years ago by announcing steps to create a multilateral network for supervising global markets and financial institutions.
In addition, the Denver summit will endorse a broad international effort to promote development in Africa, Summers said. That will include an attempt to ease access to markets for African products.
The summit members will also try to agree on methods for fighting corruption, which lies behind many banking crises around the world, Summers noted.
The G7 countries and Russia are asking nations to participate by year-end in an international convention to criminalize bribery, he noted.
Summers said Russia "has made significant progress in reshaping its economy" and said its participation in the Denver summit will reflect its increased stature in world affairs.
He repeated that the United States should swiftly pay what it owes to support international financial institutions to show of leadership in world affairs.
"It is wrong for the wealthiest country in the world to be nearly $1 billion in arrears to these institiions," Summers said.
